**Analyzing User Stories**

I'm currently dissecting the user stories for the Mule ESB project. My focus is on understanding the nuances of each story, starting with U1, which involves configuring the NIO stack through `deploy.properties`. This initial analysis is crucial for building an accurate WBS.

**Developing WebSocket Integration**

I'm continuing to refine my understanding of the Mule ESB user stories. My current focus is on the technical and design decisions for integrating WebSocket components, specifically extending the transport layer for NIO selector support and implementing the Registry client module for account pairing.

**Implementing Advanced Features**

I'm now focusing on the dynamic routing of deployed app HTTP endpoints against the Registry API, along with enforcing local flow endpoint throttling. I'm also preparing to enhance the business event subsystem for custom event formatting and upgrade MVEL dependencies with regression testing. Additionally, I plan to add JDBC connection helpers for various databases and implement SQL query logging.

**Structuring Project Tasks**

I am now detailing the specific activities required to complete the project. My current focus is on breaking down the implementation of the NIO stack and WebSocket components, followed by the registry account pairing and HTTP endpoint auto-registration. I'm also planning the implementation for the dynamic lookup component and throttling policy enforcement.

**Enhancing Project Components**

I'm now focusing on implementing custom business event logging and upgrading the MVEL library. Following that, I'll be configuring various database connectors and enabling debug-level SQL query logging. Integration testing will then tie these advancements together.

**Implementing Advanced Features**

I'm also preparing to enhance the business event subsystem for custom event formatting and upgrade MVEL dependencies with regression testing. Additionally, I plan to add JDBC connection helpers for various databases and implement SQL query logging.

**Structuring Project Tasks**

I am now detailing the specific activities required to complete the project. My current focus is on breaking down the implementation of the NIO stack and WebSocket components, followed by the registry account pairing and HTTP endpoint auto-registration. I'm also planning the implementation for the dynamic lookup component and throttling policy enforcement.

technical_and_design_decisions: Extend the Mule connector framework to include dedicated WebSocket inbound and outbound endpoint components that use an underlying NIO transport stack, toggleable via deploy.properties.
Develop a Registry integration module that securely stores the registry key, listens to application lifecycle events, and registers/manages HTTP endpoints with the configured Registry instance.
Implement a Dynamic Router message processor capable of dynamically resolving dynamic endpoints against the Registry service at runtime.
Create a runtime throttling policy filter/interceptor component applied to Mule endpoints as specified by Registry policies.
Extend the event tracking and logging framework to intercept custom business events and transaction IDs and format them for stdout/log files during application execution.
Upgrade MVEL dependency in Maven build files to 2.1.8 and execute regression tests across DataMapper and Mule expression evaluators.
Extend database connector metadata and default configurations to support connection templates for Oracle, PostgreSQL, Sybase, MS SQL Server, and DB2.
Implement a JDBC statement wrapper/interceptor that checks log level configuration and logs execute SQL queries when set to DEBUG.
assumptions: Registry API specifications for authentication, endpoint registration, endpoint lookup, and policy retrieval are available via internal documentation.
Database drivers for target vendors (Oracle, PostgreSQL, Sybase, MS SQL Server, DB2) are available in accessible repositories for integration testing.
Development and testing will be performed by a single developer with strong familiarity with Mule ESB architecture.
Effort estimates include design, implementation, unit testing, integration testing, and technical documentation updates.

activities.activity_name: NIO Stack Toggle & WebSocket Component Implementation (U1)
activities.activity_description: Add support for reading NIO configuration from deploy.properties, implement NIO transport hooks, and create WebSocket flow components (inbound/outbound).

activities.activity_name: Registry Account Pairing & HTTP Endpoint Management (U2)
activities.activity_description: Implement registry key configuration handling and deploy-time lifecycle listener to automatically register and manage deployed application HTTP endpoints with the Registry.
Build the dynamic router flow component supporting dynamic endpoint lookup and resolution through the paired Registry API.
Develop endpoint interceptor components to enforce throttling policies defined in and retrieved from the Registry.

activities.activity_name: Custom Business Events & Transaction ID Logging (U5)
activities.activity_description: Enhance event notifications to extract and format custom business events and transaction IDs to Mule system logs during local development.
Update MVEL dependencies to version 2.1.8, adapt DataMapper and expression parsing layers as needed, and verify expression evaluation stability.
Add out-of-the-box configuration helpers and connection providers for Oracle, PostgreSQL, Sybase, MS SQL Server, and DB2.
Implement a query interceptor in the database transport layer to output full SQL statements to standard Mule logs when log level is set to DEBUG.
Conduct end-to-end integration testing across all updated subsystems, resolve regression issues, and prepare documentation.
